subject.summary: A data construct of one run of NetLogo's Simple Viral Marketing model: the floor is a 500-person social network, height is time, and the cascade of adoption rises from the floor. Around the rim stand the 54 people with no links, reached only by advertising, whose spikes keep rising long after everyone else has adopted.

facts.value: One run of NetLogo's Simple Viral Marketing model

One run of NetLogo's Simple Viral Marketing model (Uri Wilensky, 2012; IABM Textbook, chapter 8) in NetLogo 7.0.4: an Erdos-Renyi random network of 500 people (link probability 0.004), the 3 people with the highest betweenness centrality seeded, random-seed 2026. Each tick a person who has not adopted adopts with probability 0.01 (advertising), or else with probability 0.5 x the share of their neighbours who have adopted. The run ended at tick 470, when everyone had adopted.

Y is up. The floor (y = 0) is the social network: NetLogo's spring layout, scaled into a disc of radius 9; the 54 people with no links stand evenly on a ring of radius 11. Height is time: a person's point is at h = 14 * sqrt(tick / 470), so the build, which rises from the floor, reaches each person when they adopted.

For a person convinced by neighbours, the cascade line comes from one neighbour who had already adopted, chosen at random: a drawing choice. The model's rule uses the share of adopted neighbours, not one person.
Floor network, cascade, advertising threads, isolated comb and seeds from the simulation run; the credited neighbour is a drawing choice.
